svg.title: The ladder of output guarantees, and what each rung leaves to you
svg.desc: A hand-drawn ladder of four rungs, strongest at the top. Grammar-constrained decoding gives validity by construction: the schema compiles to a state machine and every token that would break validity is masked before sampling, leaving only semantic validity to you. A strict response_format gives a provider-enforced shape from a JSON Schema of names, types, required keys, and enums, leaving semantic validity and setting additionalProperties to false. Tool-call arguments give the same provider-enforced shape because a tool's parameters field is a JSON Schema, and additionally leave you a trace that reads as an action rather than an answer. An instruction in the prompt asking for JSON is best-effort only and leaves you everything: preambles, code fences, trailing commas, single quotes, and truncation. Captions note that strictness at the schema is cheaper than defensiveness at every call site, and that truncation is a budget interaction.
